extractor_notes: TRANSMISSIONS: the source gives one slot ('14:30 weekday') and states that the service has a '+1 timeshift channel'. I have therefore recorded two transmissions. The 15:30 start_time for t2 is derived from the meaning of '+1' and is not stated verbatim in the source; the derivation is also listed in not_stated so a reviewer can confirm it. No date is given for either, only 'weekday', so date is not_stated for both; the prompt treats a time without a date as a finding in itself. runtime_minutes is taken as 22 from the title line '(sitcom, 22 min episode)'. existing_certificates is an empty array because the source says 'CERTIFICATE: none'; note that this is a positive assertion of absence rather than missing information, which is why it is an empty list rather than an unknown. OBSERVATION: the 00:11:40 entry is recorded once, as sexual_content. is_depicted is false: the source states twice that nothing is shown ('No sexual activity is shown and no nudity is visible') and that the sex is established only through dialogue, so what is depicted is the aftermath, not the act. The aftermath itself (two people in bed under a duvet) is shown, so a reviewer may read is_depicted differently; the full text of what is and is not shown is preserved in what_happens, descriptors and evidence so the distinction is not lost. treatment is 'fictional' because the asset is identified as a sitcom; I have not used 'comedic' because the source does not say that this particular scene is played for laughs, only that the programme is a sitcom, and the prompt requires treatment to record what the description supports. No nudity observation is recorded, since the source states no nudity is visible. is_news_or_current_affairs is set to 'no' on the basis of the stated descriptor 'sitcom'. is_made_primarily_for_children is left not_stated: the source says 'general entertainment', which is not a statement about a child audience, and the prompt forbids inferring this flag from genre or tone.
